strategy_name: Double Red — two consecutive bearish candles after a resistance test
setup_summary: On a 5-min chart, after price tests a resistance level, wait for two consecutive bearish candles where the second closes lower than the first; enter a short (Put) at the close of the second bar with a horizon of 5-15 bars. Thesis is falsifiable: two lower-lower closes after a resistance tag, no wick or structure-break requirement.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: resistance test followed by two bearish bars, second closing below the first. Invalidated/blocked if the market is highly volatile or a major scheduled news event is imminent (book: 'Not suited for volatile markets. Do not use it when big news events are taking place.'); thesis dead if price reclaims back above the first red bar's high.
risk_geometry: Entry: next bar close after the second lower close (book's binary Put). No stop/target given; expiry 5-15 min in binary terms, which translates to an expiry_bars horizon. Regime gate: skip volatile markets and news windows.
quote: The double red strategy is a short-term reversal system based on price action and resistance. The trade is planned on a 5-minute chart and is signaled when two bearish candles form following a test of resistance.
chapter_anchor: Strategies #1: The Double Red Strategy
mechanism: Two lower closes after a resistance rejection confirm seller control and predict continued downward drift; the resistance test gives the level a location anchor.
notes: Candidate behavior family requiring a resistance-label feature (windowed extremes). Closest existing V8 family is failed_breakout (liquidity_vacuum_reentry); Double Red could be tested as a 2-bar-confirmation variant of it, but its mechanism claim (rejection momentum, no prior breakout failure) is distinct. The news/volatility gate is weaker in crypto perps (24/7, no single scheduled event, though high-impact macro releases do hit BTC).
book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

strategy_name: Kangaroo tail recoil
mechanism: a single-bar rejected price extreme protruding from congestion creates recoil back into the zone
setup_summary: A single bar protrudes from a compact congestion area, leaving a long wick (a 'kangaroo tail') that marks a rejected high or low; markets tend to recoil away from the tail. Tail pointing up -> sell (or take profits on longs); tail pointing down -> buy. The stop is placed midway down the tail, not below its tip, because a stop below the tip exposes the trade to too much risk. After the tail, one may add on the next bar that trades in the trade direction and take profits when the move stalls.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalidates if price closes back beyond the tail's extreme (rejection fails and the level holds); recoil is expected away from the tail direction back into the congestion zone.
risk_geometry: Entry: on the bar trading away from a tail protruding from congestion, with optional add on the next bar in the trade direction; stop: midway down the tail (book explicitly prohibits a stop below the tip as too wide); target: take profits when the move stops making new highs (longs) / new lows (shorts), i.e. opposite side of congestion.
quote: Tails show that either a high or a low price level has been rejected by the mass of market participants. Since markets tend to move away from rejected price levels, it pays to trade in the direction opposite a tail.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3 (Classical Chart Analysis), Q 3-12, 3-13; Answers 3-12, 3-13
notes: Distinct from the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert (which requires the wick extreme to be a windowed prior extreme reclaimed by close): kangaroo tail is a single-bar rejection from within compact congestion with a distinctive stop-at-mid-tail rule. Book notes some vehicles are more tail-prone than others (Answer 3-12). On perp crypto, long wicks are often liquidation cascades rather than pure rejection, so the mechanism may need a venue-microstructure qualifier before formalizing; test as a challenger variant of sweep_reclaim first.
book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

strategy_name: Hammer bottom-reversal at support
mechanism: long lower wick shows the market sold off intra-session then was bought back to close near the high; buyers rejected lower prices at the hammer's low
setup_summary: After a downtrend (ideally confirming a prior support level or an oversold condition), a 1h bar prints a small real body (black or white) at the top of the bar's range, little or no upper shadow, and a lower shadow at least 2x the height of the real body. Buy on the hammer bar's close with a stop under the low of the hammer's lower shadow; the hammer low acts as support, and the first bounce may fail and retest it.
trigger_invalidation: Dead-thesis is a close under the hammer's low (an intraday wick under is not enough); a hammer not preceded by a downtrend is not a hammer (shape alone is insufficient - the trend defines the pattern).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close of the hammer session (V8: NEXT_BAR_CLOSE). Stop: below the frozen low of the hammer's lower shadow (swing ref). Target: prior resistance / falling resistance line / prior pivot high - candles give no targets. Expiry not stated; book notes first bounce after a hammer often fails and retests the hammer's low before a real rally.
quote: A hammer gives a potent signal when it appears after a significant downtrend or in an oversold market... there may be selling on a rally from the hammer. Therefore, the first bounce after the hammer may fail, and the market may return to test the hammer's support.
chapter_anchor: Ch2 S1 (pp.30-41) + Ch4/Ch6 worked examples (buy on hammer close, stop under hammer low, p.117, p.191)
notes: Distinct from existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim: hammer is defined by body/shadow ratios (lower shadow >= 2x body, small body at top of range), not by sweeping a windowed prior extreme. The hammer low is a natural frozen ref usable as both stop and still_valid pivot. Fills-at-close make the 'buy on hammer close' entry clean.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Engulfing-pattern top/bottom reversal
mechanism: one session's real body completely wraps the prior opposite-color real body, showing supply overwhelmed demand (bearish) or demand overwhelmed supply (bullish)
setup_summary: Bearish: in an uptrend, a black bar's real body completely wraps the prior white bar's real body (only the real body must be engulfed, shadows may exceed). Short on that bar's close; the high of the pattern is resistance. Bullish: in a downtrend, a white bar wraps the prior black bar; long on close; the pattern's lows are support. Context rule is strict: the engulfing combination after the wrong trend is not a reversal signal.
trigger_invalidation: A close beyond the engulfing bar's opposite extreme negates (e.g., close above pattern high for a short = resistance broken). Engulfing after a decline (not a rally) for the bearish variant is explicitly NOT a signal - context, not shape, makes the pattern.
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the engulfing bar. Stop: beyond the opposite extreme of the pattern (above pattern high for shorts, below pattern lows for longs). Target: structure (box bottom/top, prior S/R, falling resistance line) since candles give no targets. The book's real-world demo shorts a box range from a gravestone-doji/engulfing top at 420 to the box bottom at 370.
quote: If the market is solid, the lows of the bullish engulfing pattern should be support. Thus, for those who are long based on this pattern, there should be a stop under the lows of this pattern.
notes: The book repeats the context rule many times and shows cases where the exact same candle combination is NOT a reversal because the prior trend was wrong - a strong spec-level lesson for pattern classifiers. Volume confirmation (light volume on the engulfed bar, spike on the engulfing bar) strengthens the signal.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Change of polarity: old resistance becomes new support
mechanism: price memory: once a level is broken by a committed close, participants who missed the move buy the first retest of the flipped level; old S/R inverts role
setup_summary: After the market closes above a multi-tested resistance area, that prior resistance zone becomes new support; buy the first retest that holds on a close basis. Symmetrically, a close below prior support turns that zone into resistance; sell the retest that fails to close above it.
trigger_invalidation: For a long on flipped support: a close back inside/under the old resistance zone invalidates the flip (close-based, not intraday poke).
risk_geometry: Entry: retest of the flipped zone holding on a close (V8: NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after the retest bar). Stop: below/above the flipped zone (a defined swing ref). Target: next S/R level or structure.
quote: Once a market breaks over a multitested resistance area, the prior resistance area is converted into new support. In contrast, markets that fall through prior support have trouble climbing back through it again since that previous support is frequently converted into resistance.
chapter_anchor: Ch1 S3, pp.23-24 (Exhibit 1.7)
notes: Nison explicitly labels this not a Japanese technique but a core principle of technical analysis. Horizontal level flips are directly constructible from 1h BTCUSDT marketstate location features and are corroborated across the library. Candidate family: supply_demand_zone.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Ichimoku bar-count time elements (9/17/26/33/42/.../257 cycles) and Gann square-of-odds
setup_summary: Place vertical lines at swing-reversal bars (>=2 bars of higher-highs/lower-lows), then measure bar-count distances between all reversal pairs; count a match if the distance equals one of the derived numbers (9,17,26,33,42,51,65,76,83,97,101,129,172,200,257) or +/-1. Book author admits he does not even use these (prefers W.D. Gann), that during a sustained 18-week trend there was 'really no match', that ranges around the values cover almost all numbers ('do not use a range'), and that 'time elements by themselves are not too valuable'.
trigger_invalidation: No reliable trigger; author uses them only as calendar alerts then applies discretionary technical analysis. Poor falsifiability: +/-1 tolerance plus many candidate numbers near-guarantee hindsight matches (multiple-comparisons problem).
risk_geometry: None.
quote: The time elements indicate a possible price reversal. Time elements by themselves are not too valuable.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6 'Ichimoku Time Elements' (pp.161-170)
notes: REJECT for V8: (a) author self-reports weak performance and non-use; (b) weekend/calendar dependence is ambiguous in a 24/7 market where every hour trades; (c) the +/-1 tolerance + 15 candidate numbers make the pattern unfalsifiable ex-ante. If anything, keep only as a lesson against multi-hypothesis cycle fitting. W.D. Gann square-of-odd-number time projections share the same falsifiability problem.
book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement/extension levels
setup_summary: Chapters 8-9 (pp.129-159) cover the 'Fibonacci retracement and extension ratio relationship' (pp.140-146), with retracement levels cited in reference to support and resistance (pp.142, 144) and 'fibonacci levels' (pp.143, 149). Falsifiable: price tends to halt or reverse at Fibonacci ratios (retracements) and project to extensions (targets) of prior legs. Notably, the book itself titles Ch.9 'The Reality of the Fibonacci Secret', signaling a self-critical, potentially falsifying chapter.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price pulls back to a Fib level of a prior leg. Invalidation: price closes through the Fib level with no reaction, or level spacing is violated by the observed data.
risk_geometry: Entry at Fib retracement levels; extensions used as targets; the index notes Fibonacci ratios in reference to both support and resistance.
quote: The Fibonacci Retracement and Extension Ratio Relationship, 140
chapter_anchor: Index pp.129-159 (Ch.8 The Fibonacci Secret; Ch.9 The Reality of the Fibonacci Secret)
notes: Fibonacci is a self-fulfilling/probabilistic heuristic with no causal microstructure claim; V8 should test it only as a location-feature hypothesis with a falsification gate. The book's own 'Reality of' chapter is a warning label.

strategy_name: Bat pattern - deep 0.886 XA retracement reversal
mechanism: a shallow B retracement (<0.618) sets up a deep 0.886 retest of the XA leg, catching longs/shorts at extreme support/resistance with a tight stop
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: B must retrace <0.618 of XA (prefer exact 0.50, or 0.382); D point at the 0.886 XA retracement; BC projection must be >=1.618 (ideal 1.618 or 2.0; 1.27 invalidates); AB=CD minimum completion, Alternate 1.27 AB=CD most common; C retrace 0.382-0.886. The 0.886 is the defining PRZ level. Book claims smaller stop loss than most patterns and sharp, quick reversals; the full PRZ tends to be tested in valid Bat reversals.
trigger_invalidation: A BC projection under 1.618 invalidates the structure; valid reversals typically test the entire PRZ (bearish Bat 'tends to test its entire PRZ in valid structures more than most other patterns'); standard blowout rules (full PRZ violation on initial test) invalidate.
risk_geometry: Entry at the 0.886 retracement (book: 'typically the optimal area to execute a trade'); stop tighter than other patterns, just beyond PRZ; targets = IPO 0.382/0.618 retracements of pattern range.
quote: The pattern incorporates the powerful 0.886 XA retracement, as the defining element in the PRZ.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'The Bat Pattern', pp. 71-96
notes: 0.886 (4th root of 0.618) is a genuine numerical anchor that can be implemented as a frozen-ratio retracement feature. The B-point (<0.618) vs Gartley (0.618) distinction is the family-differentiator the book stresses most.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Gartley pattern - precise 0.618 B point with 0.786 D retracement
mechanism: a mandatory precise 0.618 B retracement of XA validates a 5-point correction whose D completes at the 0.786 XA retracement overlapped by an equivalent AB=CD
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: B must be a precise 0.618 retracement of XA (most precise B point requirement of all patterns - deviation produces a 'deeper' Bat-like structure); D at 0.786 XA retracement; BC projection must NOT exceed 1.618 (1.13-1.618); equivalent AB=CD completion is mandatory and its overlap with the 0.786 retracement typically defines the critical PRZ level; C retrace 0.382-0.886.
trigger_invalidation: BC projection >1.618 indicates a Bat, not a Gartley; the equivalent AB=CD + 0.786 overlap is the defining zone, and the reversal often fires off that overlap even before the full PRZ is tested; blowout rules apply.
risk_geometry: Entry in the PRZ (book: 'a distinct window of opportunity'); the AB=CD completion and 0.786 retracement are the most critical numbers; X-point stop for retracement patterns; IPO 0.382/0.618 targets.
quote: the Gartley must possess a precise 0.618 B point retracement to validate the structure
chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'The Gartley Pattern', pp. 97-120
notes: The B-point tolerance band is the falsifiable parameter: book says anything below ideal 0.618 alignment favors a Bat completion instead. Useful as a variant-of-family discriminator in V8's one-family-one-multiplicity-unit model.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Prior harmonic support/resistance polarity flip after violation
mechanism: violated harmonic PRZs flip polarity: prior support becomes future resistance and prior resistance becomes future support on the retest
setup_summary: After a harmonic PRZ is clearly violated, record the full PRZ band as a frozen level; on the eventual retest (book: 'it is common for price action to retest these harmonic levels'), the band acts as the opposite-polarity S/R. Book example: NQ intraday bullish Bat violated at 1780, later retested and acted as resistance; SMH gapped through a Deep Bearish Crab, retraced, and the prior resistance zone acted as support while the gap filled.
trigger_invalidation: Only well-defined prior patterns count ('these situations are most commonly found when a pattern has been clearly violated'); retest must behave like the opposite-polarity level (reject on first touch) or it is not a valid flip.
risk_geometry: Zone-based retest entries; no explicit stops/targets stated beyond standard PRZ management.
quote: When support is violated, that price level becomes future resistance. When resistance is violated, that price level becomes future support.
chapter_anchor: Ch 12 'Prior Harmonic Support and Resistance', pp. 246-250
notes: Classic S/R flip, corroborated across many TA books; for V8 this is a location-feature input: frozen violated-zone bands (like failed_breakout's prior_high_ref) plus a polarity flag. Gap-fill note is perp-relevant: SMH example = gap fill at prior resistance, analogous to funding/liquidation-driven fills back to levels.

strategy_name: Harmonic Trade Management System - IPO/PPZ/SLZ/0.382 trailer
mechanism: all trade parameters (entry, initial profit, protection, stop) are defined relative to the pattern structure in advance, letting price signals rather than emotion manage the position
setup_summary: After a PRZ entry: (1) Initial Profit Objective (IPO) = 0.382 or 0.618 retracement of the pattern range (pattern high to reversal low for bullish); if the reversal blows through 0.382, target 0.618. (2) Split the position and bank partial profit at the IPO so half 'rides for free'. (3) Profit Protection Zone (PPZ) - 'never let a profit become a loss': defend small profits until the equivalent time projection is reached. (4) Stop Loss Zone (SLZ) beyond the PRZ. (5) 0.382 trailing stop after the IPO: cover when price retraces past the 38.2% level of the reversal move. Trend-line breaks are additional exits; stalling at an IPO with no continuation = cover.
trigger_invalidation: Book rule: 'If in doubt, get out'; lack of continuation at an IPO is 'a sign of temporary exhaustion that must be respected'; the 0.382 trailer violation is the make-or-break cover trigger.
risk_geometry: Entry per pattern; initial target = 0.382/0.618 of pattern range; protection = PPZ (defend profit until 1.0 time); stop = SLZ beyond PRZ then 0.382 trailer; book-stated partial-position scaling (2-3 portions) at the IPO levels.
quote: Never let a profit become a loss.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'The Harmonic Trade Management System', pp. 203-232 (IPO p. 205, PPZ p. 206, SLZ p. 207, 0.382 trailer p. 207)
notes: Directly transferable to V8 risk_geometry: targets as structure-relative retracements (not R-multiples), frozen-ratio trailing stop, and partial scaling. The IPO-at-0.382/0.618 rule gives V8 a concrete alternative target rule to the current fixed target_r=1.0. Book admits the same pattern yields different outcomes - management rules, not pattern accuracy, are the edge claim.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Fibonacci time projections - minimum 0.382 time filter and 1.0 equivalent time
mechanism: a pattern's CD leg should not complete before the minimum 0.382 time projection (relative to X-to-B duration), and significant reversals often accelerate only after the equivalent (1.0) time projection is reached
setup_summary: Measure the X-to-B time duration (bars); project Fibonacci time targets (0.382...1.0) from B to the D completion. Rule 1: a pattern completing before 0.382 of projected time is suspect ('a red flag... the validity of the setup must be considered suspect'). Rule 2: price is primary - never require time for entry, only filter ('the key is to execute in the PRZ, as long as the minimum 0.382 time objective has been reached'). Rule 3: defend small profits until the 1.0 equivalent time is reached, after which breakouts tend to accelerate.
trigger_invalidation: CD leg completes in far less than 0.382 of the XB time -> invalidate/suspect; no meaningful move by the equivalent time -> cover the small profit.
risk_geometry: No price geometry; pure expiry/validity timing: min 0.382 bar-count floor and a 1.0-count decision gate for defending the PPZ.
quote: At a minimum, a pattern should not complete until it has reached the 0.382 time projection.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Time Considerations', pp. 208-209; worked examples pp. 213-225
notes: For 24/7 continuous tape this is cleanly computable from bar counts (no session/gap distortion). Book explicitly subordinates time to price: 'the time requirement for a pattern's completion is not as important as the price objective.' Maps to V8 expiry_bars with a minimum-bar-count validity filter.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Pattern differentiation and price-over-time discipline ('all patterns are not the same')
mechanism: similar-looking 5-point structures are distinct technical entities with different ratio alignments and different management; trading them via a pre-defined rule system (entry/stop/target all set in advance) removes emotional discretion
setup_summary: Methodology lessons: (1) do not treat Bat/Gartley/Crab/Butterfly as interchangeable - B-point ratio and D-point ratio define the family; (2) price is primary, time secondary - execution follows the price zone not the time projection; (3) every possible outcome (reversal, stall, blowout) has a pre-planned response (the Action/Task model); (4) keep a written trade journal + execution checklist (pattern present? AB=CD? >=3 numbers converging? warning signs? stop level? risk willing?).
trigger_invalidation: No setup-level trigger; the lesson is that missing the exact alignment (e.g., labeling a Bat as a Gartley) is itself the failure mode the book warns against.
risk_geometry: All parameters defined relative to structure before entry; 'the price of the next tick' as the cost of waiting for confirmation.
quote: all patterns are not the same
chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Fibonacci Pattern Alignments', p. 37; Ch 9 'Trade Execution' (checklist p. 180, journal p. 179)
notes: V8 already encodes this: one behavior family per expert, ratio-alignment variants as multiplicity units. The actionable lessons: enforce a ratio-tolerance band before formalizing a family, and require all risk_geometry to be frozen at candidate-generation time. Also book's honesty note ('not end-all-be-all... most pattern completions yield sizeable but temporary price moves') is directly compatible with V8's NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM stance.

strategy_name: AB=CD measured-move completion
mechanism: harmonic swing legs repeat in length; CD completes at a price that can be projected from AB and the BC retracement ratio
setup_summary: On any timeframe (book examples 5m to daily), identify three swing legs: AB impulse, BC retracement that completes between 0.382 and 0.786 of AB (measured on swing highs/lows), then CD resuming the AB direction. Project D = C +- (AB x 1.00/1.272/1.618). Pattern is valid only if BC does not exceed 1.00 x AB and D exceeds B. Enter with a limit order just beyond the projected D (shaded), expecting price to reverse and trade back to retracements of the AD swing.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches projected D after a valid ABC structure. Invalidations: BC retracement exceeds 1.00 of AB; D fails to exceed B; warning signs at C (gap in direction of D, wide range bar ~2x normal, CD made in far fewer bars than AB) signal D will overshoot to 1.272/1.618 rather than 1.00.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit order shaded just beyond D. Stop: fixed points (e.g., 5 points on S&P E-mini) or beyond a swing point. Targets: first = .618 retracement of AD, second = .786 retracement of AD; scale out 2-3 parts, move stop to breakeven after first target. Typical legs 5-8 bars; CD in fewer bars implies extension.
quote: The AB=CD pattern is a measured move where the CD leg is similar in length to the AB leg.
chapter_anchor: Ch 4, AB=CD Pattern Structure
notes: Fully implementable on BTCUSDT 1h OHLCV with swing-pivot detection and Fibonacci projection; no gap dependency (the gap-based CD-extension warning sign is absent in 24/7 markets, but the wide-range-bar variant remains measurable). The book cites Gartley's ~70% correctness claim and '40 years of testing' but presents no reproducible statistics.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Three Drives exhaustion
mechanism: three evenly spaced, successively higher/lower drives with 1.272/1.618 inter-drive extensions mark the final push before a reversal or a deeper correction
setup_summary: Three evenly spaced tops (uptrend) or bottoms (downtrend), each drive-to-drive distance a 1.272 or 1.618 extension of the prior; contains an embedded AB=CD with retracements at A and C ideally at .618/.786; near-perfect time symmetry (legs ~equal bars or a Fibonacci ratio of bar counts). Entry at drive 3 completion; signals either a major reversal or the end of a swing/correction.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: drive 3 completes at the projected 1.272/1.618 level. Invalidated: drive ordering broken (drive 2 not between 1 and 3); C beyond A / B beyond D; extensions past 1.618 while forming; large gaps toward drive 3 completion (trend not exhausting).
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at drive-3 completion (1.272/1.618). Stop: below recent swing low / beyond the 1.618, or fixed (e.g., $2.00/share QQQQ, 5 points E-mini). Target 1 = amount risked; then .618 retracement of the swing; reversal setups allow 3-part scale-outs with extension targets.
quote: It consists of three evenly spaced tops in an uptrend or three evenly spaced bottoms in a downtrend.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Three Drives Pattern Description
notes: Structurally distinct from Butterfly (three-drive spacing symmetry vs single XA-extension) but same exhaustion-reversal family and same failure mode (continuation moves when it fails, e.g., gold failed-sell setup where price rose $125). Falsifiable via swing labelling but contrarian profile warrants backlog status.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Head and Shoulders neckline break with measured target
mechanism: a three-swing reversal structure (left shoulder - head - right shoulder) whose neckline break resolves the pattern; height projection gives a measured target
setup_summary: Left shoulder, head, right shoulder; the countertrend rally into the right shoulder usually retraces .618/.786 of the head swing (lower right-shoulder ratio = more bearish for a top). Entry on the neckline break (sell-stop below neckline for a top, buy-stop above for a bottom) or by fading the right-shoulder retracement. Measured target = pattern height projected from the broken neckline; alternate target = 1.272 extension of the internal AB=CD. Failure point = above the head (top) / below the head (bottom), where the move reverses and continues the original trend.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: neckline break after the right shoulder forms. Invalidated: price exceeds the head (pattern fails); right shoulder retraces beyond the left-shoulder extreme. Stand-aside if pattern is only visible late.
risk_geometry: Entry: sell/buy-stop at neckline or limit at right-shoulder .618/.786. Stop: above head (top) or visual point/dollar amount; manage to breakeven after partial. Target 1: pattern-height projection from neckline; target 2: 1.272 extension of AD of embedded AB=CD, then trail.
quote: Another traditional way to measure a profit objective with this pattern is to take the height of the pattern and project it down from the price level of the broken neckline.
chapter_anchor: Ch 9, Trading the Head and Shoulders Top Pattern
notes: Swing-structure pattern implementable on 1h BTC (shoulder/head/neckline detection + measured projection). Note in crypto the neckline is often tested repeatedly and stop placements cluster there, so the breakout quality signal matters. Book notes left shoulders often contain Butterfly/AB=CD structures that can be traded directly.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Round-number and prior-cluster support/resistance with role reversal
mechanism: Traders who traded a level before re-enter at it on retests (longs add, shorts cover) making it support; after a break both groups flip to sellers, so the level reverses role; round numbers act as psychological anchors
setup_summary: Mark horizontal levels at round numbers and prior swing clusters; buy close to support, sell close to resistance; a broken level flips role (former support becomes resistance). Book examples: USDJPY 101-102 was a multi-decade support zone (1993 low 101.10, 1999 low 101.26, 2005 low 101.67); USDCAD 1.1700 was support in Nov 2004 and became resistance in Jan/Mar 2006 and Jan/Mar 2007.
trigger_invalidation: A level holds only while sentiment supports it ('bearish sentiment ensured that the buying was not sufficient enough to hold 1.1700'); invalidated on a decisive break-and-reversal-of-role, at which point the level trades as its opposite.
risk_geometry: Entry: at/close to the zone; stop: beyond the zone; no explicit target in book.
quote: The zone surrounding 2.0000 was resistance for the GBPUSD as the 1991 high was at 1.9990, the 1992 high was at 2.0035, and the January 2007 was at 1.9914.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Support and Resistance, pp. 105-108
notes: BTC round levels (100k, 50k, etc.) are widely watched in perp order books and produce clustering; add round-number proximity and prior-swing-cluster proximity as location features. Role-reversal after a break is a falsifiable behavior for the location feature group.
book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement/projection support-resistance
mechanism: price tends to retrace or rebound to Fibonacci ratios of the prior swing, and clusters of projection lines mark stronger support/resistance; the 50% level acts as a gravity zone
setup_summary: After a significant swing, mark retracement levels 23.6/38.2/50/61.8/78.6 of that swing; expect price to hold at the first test of each level (book Fig 4.29 shows a rebound at every first test). Use Fibonacci projections (61.8/100/161.8/200/238.2 of Wave A/B swings) and treat areas where multiple projection lines cluster as stronger SR. Falsifiable: first-touch reaction at a fib level (measured as a multi-bar reversal) occurs more often than chance.
trigger_invalidation: A close through the level with increased volume voids the level (support/resistance flip).
risk_geometry: Entry at the fib level; stop beyond the level; targets at the next cluster of projections.
quote: at every first test of prices at these support levels, prices make a rebound
chapter_anchor: Ch 4 'Fibonacci Retracement and Projection' and 'Appendix: Ratios and Wave Relationship'
notes: Self-fulfilling component (many traders use the same levels); crypto reacts to round/psychological numbers, so stickiness is plausible but needs evidence-gated testing.

strategy_name: AB=CD / Gartley harmonic retracement
mechanism: Harmonic price structures complete at Fibonacci ratio levels (0.382/0.618/1.618); the AB=CD structure projects a target completion where the CD leg equals AB, creating a reversal point at D.
setup_summary: Identify a four-leg swing structure: leg AB, retracement BC, and leg CD where CD equals AB in length (and BC retraces AB at a Fibonacci ratio, commonly ~0.618); the completion point D is the reversal/entry zone. Gartley pattern is the indexed variant.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: D completes at the AB-equality projection and/or Fibonacci retracement of the larger leg. Invalidation: price extends through D by a defined threshold (structure failed).
risk_geometry: Entry at completion point D; standard stop beyond D (not stated in this part); targets from Fibonacci ratios 0.382/0.618/1.618.
quote: The important ratios are 0.382, 0.618, and 1.618.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Fibonacci ratios; Glossary: A-B-C correction; Index: AB=CD patterns, Gartley Pattern (AB=CD pattern)
notes: Requires swing-point labeling; concretely falsifiable once peaks/troughs are programmatically identified. Gartley book is cited in the bibliography (Profits in the Stock Market), giving literature corroboration.
book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

strategy_name: Rule of Equality: extended-wave target projection
mechanism: In Elliott Wave five-wave structure, when one impulse wave extends, the remaining two impulse waves tend to be equal in length - a Fibonacci-ratio equality that yields objective price targets for the non-extended waves.
setup_summary: After labeling a five-wave impulse in which one wave (commonly wave 3) is extended, project the length of the extended wave onto the other impulse waves as equality targets (Rule of Equality); use 0.382/0.618/1.618 retracement and projection levels as entry/target zones.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extended impulse wave identified. Invalidation: subsequent waves fail to approximate the equality projection (structure invalidated by a new extreme beyond the projected target).
risk_geometry: Target-setting only: projection = length of extended wave mapped to remaining impulse waves; levels 0.382/0.618/1.618 as retracement/projection anchors.
quote: When one impulse wave is extended in a five-wave structure, the remaining two waves tend to be equal.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Equality, Rule of; Glossary: extended wave; Index: Fibonacci Retracement and Projection, Elliott Wave Theory
notes: Objective target-projection tool, but gated on subjective wave labeling; V8 should treat it as a location/target feature input (fib levels), not an autonomous expert. Rule of Alternation (Wave 2 simple -> Wave 4 complex) is the companion EW heuristic in the same glossary.

strategy_name: Hammer / Hanging man / Shooting star (single-candle rejection lines)
setup_summary: After a downtrend, a candle with a small real body near the upper end of the range, lower shadow >=3x the real body, and little/no upper shadow (hammer) is bullish. The same shape after an uptrend is a hanging man and is only bearish when the next session closes under its real body. A shooting star (long upper shadow, small body near the bottom of the range) after an uptrend is a top-reversal.
trigger_invalidation: Hanging man requires next-bar close under its real body as confirmation; the pattern candle alone is not a signal. Hammer/shooting star likewise need next-bar confirmation in the reversal direction.
risk_geometry: Entry on the confirmation bar's close, not the pattern bar; stop beyond the shadow extreme; book only references risk/reward broadly (Index p.133-137) without numeric multiples here.
quote: a long lower shadow usually three times or more the length of the real body... The hanging man and hammer have the same shape. What differentiates one from the other is that the hammer follows a downtrend while the hanging man is after an uptrend.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Hammer / Hanging man (p.259-260), Shooting star (p.267)
notes: Shape-only patterns are abundant on 1h crypto and false-positive-prone at high leverage; the trend precondition and the next-bar confirmation rule are the load-bearing, falsifiable parts.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Engulfing / Piercing / Harami / Last engulfing (dual-candle reversal family)
setup_summary: After a trend, a real body that fully engulfs the prior opposite-color body is a reversal (bullish engulfing after a decline, bearish after a rise). Weaker/exhaustion variants: piercing line (white close >=50% into the prior black body after a new low), last engulfing (the engulfing pattern that appears as the final move of the trend), and harami (small body held inside the prior long body = indecision, trend fuel fading).
trigger_invalidation: All variants need a prior trend to reverse; harami is an indecision signal requiring subsequent confirmation; invalidation = next bar continues the original trend.
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; stop beyond the engulfing pattern's extreme; no numeric R given in this section.
quote: thisa bullish candle pattern that has the same group of candle lines that form the bearish engulfing pattern (a large black candle that engulfs the prior white candle). However, the bearish engulfing pattern appears after a rising market while the last engulfing pattern appears after a falling market.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Engulfing / Last engulfing / Piercing / Harami (p.258-263, 266)
notes: The 'last engulfing' variant frames the engulfing candle as the final thrust of the trend — a usable trend-exhaustion reading for the reversal thesis.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Morning star / Evening star (three-candle star reversals)
setup_summary: Bottom (morning star): during a downtrend a long black body, then a small real body that does not touch the first body, then a long white body that closes well into the first black body. Mirror at top (evening star): long white, small non-touching body, long black closing well into the first white. Doji variants (morning/evening doji star) when the middle candle is a doji.
trigger_invalidation: Pattern completes only when the third candle closes well into the first body and the middle candle does not touch the first body; if the third candle fails to close into the first body the pattern is void.
risk_geometry: Entry after completion of the third candle's close; stop beyond the pattern's extreme; book itself flags subjectivity (Index: 'Subjectivity, morning star and, 119,120').
quote: The last session of the morning star is a long white real body that ideally should not touch the second real body. This long white real body should close well into the first candle's black real body to complete this pattern.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Evening star (p.258), Morning star (p.263)
notes: Composite 3-bar pattern with strict gapping constraints; requires hard thresholds ('close well into', body-length ratios) to be falsifiable on 1h data.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as continuation patterns and support/resistance
setup_summary: A rising window (top of the prior session's upper shadow below the low of the current lower shadow) is a bullish continuation pattern; a falling window opens when the prior session's low is above the current session's high. The window edge acts as support (rising) or resistance (falling); 'close under top of window keeps downtrend in force' is the stated invalidation line. Variants: three windows, gapping doji, two black gapping candles.
trigger_invalidation: Continuation thesis invalid when the window fills (price closes back through it); the window-edge line is the stated invalidation reference.
risk_geometry: Window edge used as a stop reference (Index: 'rising window, stops, 130-132'); volume cited as confirmation (Index: 'Volume, windows and, 96').
quote: A rising window is a bullish continuation pattern that is formed when the top of yesterday's upper shadow is under the low of the current lower shadow... Close under top of window keeps downtrend in force.
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Windows (p.270-271)
notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7, so classic overnight gaps are absent, but shadow-gaps between consecutive candles occur at session boundaries and event shocks; window levels remain PIT-computable S/R.

strategy_name: Long real-body candles as support/resistance zones
setup_summary: A long white candle (real body >=3x recent bodies, close near high) defines a support area from midway of the body down to the bottom of the lower shadow; a long black candle (body >=3x recent bodies, close near low) defines a resistance area from 50% within the candle up to the top including the upper shadow. Zones confirm support/resistance and breakout validity; change-of-polarity applies (support becomes resistance).
trigger_invalidation: Zone valid while intact as S/R; a close through the zone flips its polarity to the opposite role.
risk_geometry: Zone boundaries give concrete stop references; zone extent defined by '50% within the candle' (black) and 'midway of the candle' (white).
quote: The resistance set up by a long black candle should be from 50% within the candle up to the top of the candle (including the upper shadow)... The support should be from midway of the white candle down to the bottom of the white candle (this includes the bottom of the lower shadow).
chapter_anchor: Glossary: Long white candle / Long black candle (p.262-263)
notes: Concrete, PIT-computable zone definitions that feed V8's location feature group; corroborates the change-of-polarity principle (Index p.275).
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Hammer / hanging man / shooting star: long-shadow rejection lines gated by prior trend
mechanism: a long shadow rejecting an extreme after a one-sided move reveals exhaustion of the losing side
setup_summary: After a significant downtrend, a bar with a long lower shadow, a small real body near the top of the range and little/no upper shadow is a hammer (bullish): buy at the close or on a successful retest of the hammer's low. The identical shape after a rally is a hanging man (bearish) and needs confirmation - the next bar closing under the hanging man's real body; a close above the hanging man's high voids it. A long upper shadow with a small body near the bottom after an uptrend is a shooting star (bearish). The same shape inside a sideways range has no reversal meaning.
trigger_invalidation: Hammer: close below the hammer's low. Hanging man: close above its high (unconfirmed) or confirmed by a next-session close under its real body. Shooting star: close above its high. No prior trend = pattern void.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close or on retest; stop under the hammer's low (close-based); hanging man confirmation = next close under its real body; book suggests scaling in - light on signal, add after successful retest.
quote: If it appears from below, buy, and if appears from above, sell... as reversal signals; they need a prior trend to reverse.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Single Candle Lines', pp.56-68
notes: The trend-context gate (pattern void in ranges) is exactly a still_valid condition for a V8 expert. Springs (failed breakdown below support that reclaims) and upthrusts (failed breakout above resistance that fails) are the Western names for the same probe-and-reject action and pair naturally with the existing sweep-reclaim family.

strategy_name: Doji at extended moves: equilibrium bar, doji-as-S/R, next-session confirmation
mechanism: open approximately equals close at an extreme of a mature move: supply and demand in balance and the directional drive has stalled
setup_summary: A bar whose open and close are equal (doji) after a steep advance - especially directly after a tall white candle - is a transition signal, not an outright sell: wait 1-2 sessions for bearish confirmation. The doji's high acts as resistance; a buy stop sits above it (a close above means the market is 'refreshed' and the uptrend resumes). Symmetric for a doji after a steep decline: a subsequent white candle resolves the balance bullishly; stop under the doji's low. A doji early in a young trend or in a range is weak/neutral.
trigger_invalidation: Close above the doji high voids the bearish doji; close below the doji low voids the bullish one; a near-doji amid a run of small bodies is not significant.
risk_geometry: Confirmation wait of 1-2 bars; stop under the doji's low (bullish scenario) or above its high (bearish); the doji extreme becomes structural S/R.
quote: a doji that emerges after the mature part of an uptrend or sell-off has a greater chance of a market turn... a doji provides 'a hint of tops and bottoms'... traders should view the doji as echoing a market in transition rather than being an outright reversal pattern.
chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Doji', pp.45-50; Ch.3 'Gapping Doji', pp.106-109
notes: Gravestone doji (open/high/close near the low of the range) is the stronger top variant; the book pairs doji with ROC/divergence corroboration. On 24/7 crypto the 'next session' is simply the next 1h bar, making the confirmation rule mechanical. The confirmation gate is a strong lifecycle-rule candidate.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Engulfing patterns: body-size asymmetry determines reversal vs consolidation
mechanism: a large body fully enveloping a small opposite body demonstrates a decisive shift in supply/demand control
setup_summary: Bearish engulfing: during a rally, a black body whose range wraps the prior white body's range; bullish engulfing is the mirror after a decline. The strictest version has a small first body and a very large second body whose range includes the first candle's shadows. Reliability scales with size asymmetry - two nearly equal bodies typically resolve into a lateral band rather than a reversal (a volatility-fade signal). A bearish engulfing following a doji is especially bearish. Engulfing extremes become support/resistance.
trigger_invalidation: Close above the top of the bearish engulfing (including shadows) voids it, flipping to bullish; the same shape in a downtrend is a last-engulfing bottom (bullish), not bearish.
risk_geometry: Entry on pattern-completion close; stop on a close above/below the engulfing extremes; book example: buy pullback to bullish engulfing support, target = prior resistance, stop under the engulfing lows.
quote: the strictest definition of an engulfing pattern would be if the first candle is small and the second candle very large, and the second real body wraps around the entire first candle-including its shadows... if there are two almost equal size candles... the market may move into a lateral band, rather than reverse.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Engulfing Patterns', pp.76-85
notes: The size-asymmetry condition and the equal-size-to-consolidation prediction are both falsifiable. The stock-vs-futures definitional flexibility is moot on perps (opens are arbitrary); the after-doji warning and engulfing-as-S/R rules port directly. Harami (inverse engulfing) and last-engulfing are closely related variants kept in the same family.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Dark cloud cover / piercing pattern: depth of counter-candle penetration
mechanism: how deep a counter-candle closes into the prior body measures how completely the opposing force has reversed control
setup_summary: Dark cloud cover: after an uptrend, a tall white bar followed by a black bar that opens above the white bar's high (futures) or above the white bar's close (stocks/perps) and closes below the midpoint of the white body. Deeper penetration = more bearish; a close short of the midpoint is incomplete and requires next-session weakness for confirmation. The pattern becomes resistance (stop on a close above its high). The piercing pattern is the bullish mirror: a white bar closing more than halfway into a prior black body after a decline.
trigger_invalidation: Close above the dark-cloud high voids it; incomplete (<50% penetration) needs confirmation; the preceding trend is required for either pattern.
risk_geometry: Entry on completion close; stop on a close above the dark cloud's high; targets from Western tools (change of polarity, prior S/R); the book explicitly demonstrates skipping a trade where risk approximates reward.
quote: As a general rule, the deeper the close of the dark cloud cover's second session pushes into the white candle, the more bearish the signal.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Dark Cloud Cover' and 'The Piercing Pattern', pp.68-76
notes: The midpoint penetration rule is precisely quantifiable for a rule-based expert. The book notes dark cloud covers are more frequent than piercing patterns (fear/greed asymmetry at tops vs bottoms). Both patterns become structural S/R after completion.
book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

strategy_name: Risk/reward gating and close-confirmed structural stops (candles + Western tools)
mechanism: a signal's tradability is conditional on the ratio of structural risk to a reachable target, not on the pattern alone
setup_summary: Never execute a candle signal in isolation: define risk as a structural stop (pattern high/low, window edge, doji extreme, flipped level) and reward as a target from a Western tool (prior support/resistance, change-of-polarity level, Fibonacci/50% retracement, moving average). Only trade when the risk/reward is attractive - the book skips a morning star with $36 risk vs $15 target, and prefers a dark cloud over a 'stronger' bearish engulfing purely on risk geometry. Stops trigger on a close through structure, not on intra-session wicks.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - an admission gate, not a position; the same discipline extends to a pre-committed invalidation price for the whole market opinion ('market chameleon').
risk_geometry: Stop = structural level, close-confirmed; target = non-candle tool level; skip trades at ~1:1 or worse; candles rarely give targets so a target source must be external.
quote: unless there is an attractive risk/reward ratio at the time the candle pattern is completed, stay away from the trade.
chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Stops' and 'Risk/Reward', pp.130-137
notes: This is the book's central methodology lesson and matches V8's RiskGate + risk_geometry design: entry gated by reward/risk, and thesis invalidation (still_valid) on a close through a frozen structural reference rather than an intra-bar wick. Leveraged perps make the gate more binding, not less.

strategy_name: Support becomes resistance: the S/R role-reversal mechanism
mechanism: traders who bought at a repeatedly-holding support level are conditioned to buy again; when support finally breaks, those traders hold losing positions, and when price returns to the former level they exit at breakeven out of relief - that selling turns former support into resistance (and vice versa)
setup_summary: After a well-tested support level breaks (or a well-tested resistance breaks), expect the old level to act as the opposite pole on the return: place shorts near former support that has flipped to resistance, longs near former resistance that has flipped to support; treat S/R as AREAS not exact prices (soft targets).
trigger_invalidation: If the level is never re-tested, no trade; if price breaks back through the flipped level, the role-reversal thesis is void - 'if the reason for entering the trade is no longer valid, then the trade itself is no longer valid'.
risk_geometry: Entry via resting order above support / below resistance (don't stand in front of the freight train - never place the entry directly on the level; wait for the bounce and enter as price rises/falls away from it); stop on the far side of the level.
quote: If enough selling occurs as the price nears the former support level, the exchange rate will reverse and begin to fall. Now, the former area of support has become an area of resistance.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 10 'The Ultimate Indicator', pp.133-144
notes: This is the causal engine behind the location feature group and the failed_breakout/liquidity_sweep_reclaim experts in V8: prior-tested-and-broken levels as opposite-pole magnets, driven by trapped-position unwinding (the 'pleasure principle' - traders escape at breakeven). On perps, liquidation clusters at broken levels amplify the flip. Propose a location feature: 'windowed role-flip of prior extreme (was support, now overhead resistance)' frozen at entry.
book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

strategy_name: Tall and Wide Pattern Selection Filter
setup_summary: Among same-type chart patterns, prefer tall (height/breakout-price above the ~15-15.6% median) and wide (>37-41 days) patterns: tall double bottoms avg +44% vs +34% for short; double bottoms wider than 37 days avg +42% vs +34%; H&S bottoms both tall and wide avg +51% vs +28% (short only); tall symmetrical triangles +39% vs +24%. Small patterns underperform their large siblings.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: when screening candidate setups, compute height/breakout-price and pattern width; prefer above-median. Invalidation: none — this is a selection filter, not an entry; all figures are perfect-trade averages so individual outcomes vary.
risk_geometry: No direct entry/stop/target; informs candidate selection and, combined with the measure rule, target sizing. Large patterns also imply larger stop distances (pattern-bottom stops average ~13% loss for tall ascending triangles).
quote: Chart patterns tall and wide (large patterns) tend to perform better than narrow and short ones (small patterns).
chapter_anchor: Ch. 1 (Smart Investor Tip); Ch. 23 (Trading Setups and Tips — Height and Width)
notes: Deterministic, falsifiable filter that V8 can apply to candidate episodes; interacts with risk: tall patterns carry taller pattern-bottom stops, so the structural-stop override (see minor_low_stop_trail finding) matters.
book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

strategy_name: Exhaustion Spike Reversal (exhaustion gap / tall bar)
setup_summary: At the end of a strong trend, a high-volume exhaustion signal (gap or unusually tall bar, 2-3x the prior-month average height) appears, is NOT followed by new minor highs/lows, and price consolidates; exhaustion gaps close within ~1 week on average (9 days up / 14 days down; 64% close within a week in bull markets). The reversal after the exhaustion can be violent and is tradeable in the new direction — but the new trend often lasts only about a week, so be nimble.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: tall, high-volume spike/gap well into an established trend with no new minor extreme afterward; or a single bar 2-3x the prior-month average height (book: signals a short-term peak/valley within a day or two). Invalidation: the gap is a continuation gap instead — if price continues with little bar overlap and makes new highs/lows, it is continuation, not exhaustion; large overlap after the gap = exhaustion and time to exit.
risk_geometry: Entry: trade the new direction at the open of the bar after the exhaustion signal. Stop: beyond the spike/gap extreme. Target: gap fill / nearest support; expect the move to be short-lived (~1 week). Expiry: days.
quote: After an exhaustion gap ends, the trend reversal can be violent and offers a trading opportunity.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 (Gaps — Exhaustion gaps and gap closing stats)
notes: Crypto perps have no exchange gaps, so gap mechanics (fill, gap support) do not transfer; but tall-spike exhaustion, climax-volume reversals, and liquidation-wick reversals map directly onto V8's capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion). Tall-bar reversal clue also supports a volatility feature.

strategy_name: Triangle Apex Turning Point
setup_summary: In any triangle (ascending, descending, or symmetrical), the apex where the two converging trendlines meet is a future short-term turning point: a minor high or low occurs within ~4 days of the apex. Measured over 500 stocks (1991-1996), the average apex-to-turn distance was 3.6 days vs a 6.55-day chance benchmark; two visual tests succeeded 60% (computer-drawn) and 75% (hand-drawn) of the time. The turn is rarely a significant trend change.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: triangle identified and apex date projected; expect a short-term turn within ~4 bars. Invalidation: no minor extreme within ~4-7 bars — the apex failed; also the turn is short-lived, so do not treat it as a trend change or hold through it.
risk_geometry: Timing device: use to take profits near the apex or to time entries within ~4 bars of the apex; no stop/target given by the book. Scale-invariant (works on 1-min to monthly).
quote: The apex works as a turning point between 60 and 75 percent of the time. Look for a turn within four days of the apex. However, it will be rare that the minor high or minor low turn is a significant one (a trend change).
chapter_anchor: Ch. 26 (Triangle Apex Sell Signal); Ch. 10 (Symmetrical Triangles)
notes: Falsifiable and unusual; on 1h BTC the 4-bar window becomes an exit-timing feature rather than a standalone expert. Corroboration across books is plausible since apex-turn is a common TA claim.
book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

strategy_name: Harmonic/RSI-BAMM extension stop and first-test invalidation rule
setup_summary: For any harmonic reversal with an RSI BAMM extension: a 1.13-extended setup must not experience price beyond the 1.618 level of the final divergent move; a 1.618-extended setup must not exceed the 2.0 projection. The PRZ + RSI BAMM Confirmation Point together define a 'do or die' price level; price exceeding the stop zone - especially on the first test - invalidates the reversal and flags that the primary trend is strong.
trigger_invalidation: This IS the invalidation rule: stop zone = next extension beyond the setup's defining extension; no discretionary buffer around the level.
risk_geometry: Stop beyond the next harmonic extension (1.618 for 1.13 setups; 2.0 projection for 1.618 setups); combined with pattern PRZ violation as the earlier warning; book frames these as guidelines whose exact level depends on the pattern's PRZ.
quote: the key invalidation point truly occurs beyond the 1.618 extension of the final divergent move. The validation of the technical phenomenon becomes questionable beyond the 2.0 extension
chapter_anchor: Ch.6, pp.265-268 'Bearish RSI BAMM Failure-Stop Loss Considerations'
notes: Cleanly portable to perp crypto: the rule is a deterministic first-test violation of a frozen level (like the frozen refs in existing V8 experts), needing no exact ratio precision. Maps to RiskGate/lifecycle: stop distance defined by structural extension rather than fixed ATR multiple; also doubles as the invalidation semantics for NEW_failed_pattern_continuation.

strategy_name: Alternate Bat (shallow midpoint extension to 1.13 XA)
mechanism: A shallow midpoint (B retraces 0.382 or less of XA) predicts a deeper completion that runs stops beyond the prior extreme to the 1.13 XA extension, where the extreme BC projection (2.0-3.14) converges.
setup_summary: An M/W-type structure whose B point retraces 0.382 or less of the XA leg completes as an Alternate Bat at the 1.13 XA extension (0.886 is the minimum valid level), with BC projections at 2.0/2.618/3.14; a standard Bat completion at 0.886 would have been stopped out, whereas the 1.13 is the actual reversal level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: structure with B <=0.382 converging at the 1.13 XA extension. Invalid: price exceeds the 1.13 (that is the stop/invalidation); 0.886 is minimum support/resistance so anything shallower than that invalidates.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at 1.13 XA extension (just beyond the standard Bat PRZ); stop beyond 1.13; target: reversal into the trend; the 1.13 serves as the pattern's validation/violation limit.
quote: the Alternate Bat typically completes in the area beyond the 0.886 retracement, but it should not exceed the 1.13.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Alternate Bat Pattern'
notes: The stop-run dynamic is highly relevant to leveraged crypto (stops cluster at prior extremes and round numbers), but pattern identification needs discretion. The 1.13 invalidation is a clean, deterministic rule once swing points exist.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Stopping volume / topping-out volume absorption sequences
mechanism: in a fast waterfall the absorbing buying appears as repeated deep-lower-wick candles with high volume that close off the lows, progressively narrowing the spread until a hammer - the brakes applied; the mirror pattern at a top (deep upper wicks, high volume, arcing spreads) is topping-out/distribution.
setup_summary: After a sharp fall on rising volume (price waterfall), look for 2-3 consecutive candles with deep lower wicks, high or rising volume, closing in the upper half of the range, ending in a hammer - stopping volume; reversal/absorption is under way and a move higher is to follow. Mirror: in a mature uptrend, candles with deepening upper wicks, high/ultra-high volume and narrowing spreads (arcing) = topping-out volume; the last candle is a shooting star; distribution then selling climax.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: post-waterfall sequence of deep-lower-wick high-volume candles. Invalidation: volume keeps rising on wide down candles (no absorption; waterfall continues), or a single hammer is treated as a reversal - the book is explicit a single hammer will not halt the move.
risk_geometry: Book: close should be in the upper half of the open-close range for strength; no explicit stop/target (worked examples use the hammer wick as the stop level).
quote: The sequence of candles in Fig 6.17 is an almost perfect example, and if we do see this combination following a sharp move lower, then we would be on full alert for the forthcoming move higher.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 - Stopping Volume / Topping Out Volume
notes: Precursor sequence to the buying climax; in leveraged crypto, waterfall legs from liquidations make the stopping-volume signature (deep wicks + high volume + narrowing spread) frequent and checkable. Distinct behavior family from the single-bar climax.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Trapped-trader congestion zones as persistent support/resistance
mechanism: congestion zones are densely populated with weak, late, emotional traders trapped near the wave tops/bottoms; these trapped populations make the price region act as a self-fulfilling future support/resistance platform, and levels where the market has failed before tend to fail again.
setup_summary: Identify horizontal congestion zones (zig-zag ranges with floors and ceilings, defined by isolated pivots). Zones are elastic (breaks can be fake and price can return inside). A zone that previously failed to break is more likely to fail again; if it eventually breaks on this occasion, the level becomes a stronger platform. Buyers at the top of each wave are weak; buyers at the bottom are strong - the weak population defines the barrier.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price returning to a previously-visited, densely-traded congestion zone. Invalidation: the zone is treated as rigid (the book stresses 'rubber bands', not 'rods of steel'); significance scales with the depth/age of the zone - shallow zones matter little.
risk_geometry: The broken zone becomes a 'natural floor/ceiling' of price protection; stops go below the floor/above the ceiling of the zone; no explicit R-multiple targets.
quote: The buyers at the top of each wave can be considered to be weak, but the buyers at the bottom of each wave can be considered to be strong.
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 - Fear And Greed Riding The Wave; Support & Resistance - The House
notes: Overlaps location feature work and the liquidity_sweep family but is the zone-formation mechanism (trapped weak positions) rather than the sweep trigger; candidate companion to volume_profile for S/R significance.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Hammer/umbrella-line reversal at support with volume and oscillator confirmation
mechanism: A long lower shadow (rejection wick) at support shows buyers absorbing selling pressure after a decline; the wick marks where bids stepped in
setup_summary: After a decline, a hammer or dragonfly doji forms at a support level (prior swing low, moving average): small real body at the upper end of range, lower shadow >=2x body, no or tiny upper shadow. Confirmation: heavy volume and/or oversold stochastic. Entry at the close of the signal candle or the following bar; target is the opposite structure (e.g., SUN case: up to the April-May resistance). Mirror side: hanging man at resistance after an advance is a short setup (SUN #3 shows a hanging man was 'not significant' right after a move resumed and was negated when price closed above it).
trigger_invalidation: Signal negated when the next candle closes beyond the signal candle's extreme; low significance when it forms immediately after the trend has just resumed (context matters); weak without S/R context or volume/stochastic confirmation.
risk_geometry: Entry at signal-bar close or next-bar close; protective stop below support/swing low (sell stop for longs); target = prior resistance structure; case study cites 'an adequate reward-to-risk ratio for a short-term trade up to resistance'.
quote: An entry at the close of the doji session, or the following day, would have provided an adequate reward-to-risk ratio for a short-term trade up to resistance at the April-May highs.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN dragonfly doji at 50-SMA, #1/#8 hammer on heavy volume); Case Study 3 (WOLF #1); Appendix A Hammer / Dragonfly doji criteria
notes: Umbrella lines (hammer, hanging man, dragonfly doji) share one rejection-wick mechanism; on 1h BTC candles this is fully observable in OHLC, and 24/7 liquidation sweeps generate frequent long lower shadows at levels.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Bullish/bearish engulfing reversal at support/resistance (tweezer confluence strengthens)
mechanism: Full real-body envelopment of the prior opposite-color body in one bar marks an abrupt control shift from one side to the other
setup_summary: After a decline, a white candle whose real body completely surrounds the prior black real body = bullish engulfing (long); after an advance, a black candle surrounding the prior white body = bearish engulfing (short). The engulfing only envelops the prior real body, not necessarily its shadows. Book's cases: bullish engulfing at 50-SMA support + prior bottoms (FLR Fig 10.7), bullish engulfing at tested S/R with matching lows (tweezer bottom, MEOH #9), bearish engulfing after moves far from the average (WOLF #8).
trigger_invalidation: Pattern only confirmed at bar close (body must fully envelop prior body); mid-range engulfing without S/R context or overextension is 'not very significant' (SUN #3, WOLF #6); the tweezer alone is not significant, it only strengthens a co-occurring engulfing.
risk_geometry: Entry at signal-bar close; stop on the far side of the pattern or beyond support; target = prior resistance/structure; the engulfing day's shaven head and bottom show one-sided control (MEOH #9).
quote: It is not necessary that the second candle envelop the prior candle's upper and lower shadows, just the real body. This is a strong reversal pattern that exemplifies an abrupt turnaround in investor psychology.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 Fig 10.7 (FLR bullish engulfing at 50-SMA + prior bottoms); Ch. 11 Case Study 2 (MEOH #9 engulfing + tweezer bottom), Case Study 3 (WOLF #8); Appendix A Bearish/Bullish engulfing
notes: Body-envelopment is a purely candle-geometric test, deterministic and easy to code on 1h candles; the tweezer-strengthening condition is an additional conjunct on matching lows/highs of 2+ consecutive bars.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Piercing pattern / dark cloud cover after a gap-flush open
mechanism: A gap open against the prior move that closes deeply back into the prior body shows the flush was absorbed and control flipped to the counter-move side
setup_summary: After a decline, price gaps down open below the prior black candle's low and closes at least halfway into that black real body = bullish piercing (long). Mirror: after an advance, gap up open above the prior white candle's high and close at least halfway into the white body = dark cloud cover (short). Case studies: MEOH May 30 and July 25 piercing patterns; SUN June 4 near-dark-cloud on heavy overextension. The deeper the penetration into the prior body, the stronger the signal.
trigger_invalidation: A close that does not reach the halfway point of the prior body is 'not ideal' and weaker (SUN June 5 close was not half-way and was flagged as non-ideal); the first candle must be a strong opposite-color body; without an underlying trend or S/R the follow-through is uncertain.
risk_geometry: Entry at second-candle close; stop below the flush low (second candle's low); target = prior swing structure; penetration depth is the signal-strength scale.
quote: Price gaps down open below the prior candle's low and closes deeply (at least halfway) into the prior candle's black real body. The deeper the second candle's bullish real body penetrates the prior candle's bearish real body, the stronger the signal.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN #4 near-dark-cloud), Case Study 2 (MEOH #8, #11 piercing); Appendix A Piercing pattern / Dark cloud cover
notes: Crypto perps have no exchange gaps, but a candle that opens below the prior low after a sharp drop (flash-dip / wick flush) is observable on 1h candles; the session-open psychology of the equity 'gap' differs, so treat as an analog, not the same setup.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Morning star / evening star three-candle reversal, strength scaled by third-candle penetration and volume
mechanism: A gapped small-body indecision candle after a strong thrust, followed by a strong opposite body intruding into the thrust candle, marks exhaustion of the move
setup_summary: After a decline: a long black candle, then a small real body or doji gapping down open (the 'star'), then a white candle closing deeply into the first candle's black body = morning star (long). Mirror: evening star after an advance (short). The deeper the third candle's intrusion, the more likely the reversal follows, especially if the third candle is accompanied by heavy volume.
trigger_invalidation: Requires deep third-candle intrusion into the first candle's body; shallow intrusion or low volume weakens the signal; requires a prior trend to reverse.
risk_geometry: Entry at third-candle close; stop below the star/low; target = opposite structure; the star's gap creates the exhaustion signature.
quote: The deeper the intrusion, the more likely a reversal will follow, especially if the third candle is accompanied by heavy volume.
chapter_anchor: Appendix A Morning star / Evening star; Ch. 11 quiz answers (Fig 11.5 B, Fig 11.6 B)
notes: Rarer on 1h BTC than two-candle patterns and needs trend context; could be implemented as a variant of a single candlestick-reversal multiplicity unit (pattern type as a variant parameter) to conserve the active-expert budget.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Candlestick reversal candles as exit/lighten warnings for open positions
mechanism: A reversal candle at a stretched point marks thesis weakening; exiting or lightening before the full reversal preserves capital
setup_summary: Swing traders holding longs watch for bearish reversal signals (dark cloud cover, bearish engulfing, shooting star) to lighten or exit; shorts watch for bullish signals. Key constraint: the pattern is only identifiable at the session close, so price may already have moved against the position; mitigation is exiting early on an opening gap after a directional move, or selling part of the position on the gap and holding a protective stop on the balance. Harami signals momentum loss and 'caution' rather than an immediate reversal.
trigger_invalidation: Defensive discretion, not a hard rule: the warning candle can be a false signal; the cost of the rule is premature exit, which must be weighed against the protection.
risk_geometry: Exit at bar close on confirmed reversal candle; alternative = partial exit at the gap open plus a protective stop on the remainder.
quote: Another effective way to utilize the candlestick reversal signals is for warnings to lighten up, or exit, an open position... A challenge with utilizing the reversal signals in this manner is that you won't know until the close of the trading session that the pattern is present.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Reversal Patterns can Provide Warnings'
notes: Deterministic at bar close in V8's fill-at-close simulator; the gap-exit leg is not crypto-relevant (no gaps) but the candle-confirmed exit and lighten-on-warning logic map cleanly to episode exit rules.

strategy_name: Confluence gating: trade candlestick reversals only where S/R, volume, and oscillators add 'ammunition'
mechanism: Pattern validity is context-dependent: a reversal candle at a level with confirmation has higher follow-through than an isolated signal, so setups are selected, not all patterns traded
setup_summary: Prefer candlestick-reversal trades that form where there is additional ammunition: support/resistance (prior peaks and bottoms, moving averages), volume, and/or the stochastic oscillator. A nonideal pattern may follow through when it forms at a strong ceiling/floor, within a larger Western pattern, or after overextension, 'in spite of falling short of meeting the criteria of an ideal pattern'. Two questions before acting: (1) what price action preceded the event, (2) are there Western technical occurrences affecting direction.
trigger_invalidation: Isolated patterns with no confluence are treated as low quality; visual confluence is partly subjective, which is why the book pairs candlesticks with computable tools (volume, stochastic) for scanning.
risk_geometry: n/a - this is a setup-quality filter applied over entry rules.
quote: As long as there are many trade opportunities to choose from, I'll always gravitate toward the setups that offer a higher likelihood of following through. When I do trade based strictly on the appearance of a candlestick signal, I look for confirmation from other technical tools, such as volume and/or the stochastic oscillator.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Bullish reversal patterns formed at support' (Fig 10.7 discussion); Ch. 11 validation notes ('nonideal patterns... at a strong ceiling or floor')
notes: This is the book's central thesis and maps to V8 as a gating principle: candlestick-reversal experts should only be admitted to the expert family when location + participation + response features confirm; it also justifies the non-ideal-pattern relaxation at strong levels.
