strategy_name: Umbrella line reversal (hammer / hanging man)
mechanism: Long lower wick after a directional move shows intraday sellers exhausted and buyers recaptured price to close near the high; short-covering adds fuel for the reversal.
setup_summary: After a multi-bar directional move on BTCUSDT 1h (decline for a bullish hammer, advance for a bearish hanging man), a bar forms with a small real body at/near the top of its range, a lower shadow at least 2x the body, and no or a very small upper shadow (price closes near the range high). The signal is a reversal of the prior move; confirmation = price trades above the hammer's body (or below the hanging man's body), ideally closing there, on the following bar.
trigger_invalidation: Signal negated if the next bar instead moves in the trend's direction (e.g., a hammer followed by a lower close). A reversal pattern forming inside a consolidation has no significance because there is no move to reverse.
risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation (next-bar close above body for a hammer); initial protective stop below the pattern's low (failure point); candlesticks give no price target, so target comes from overhead structure or an R-multiple. Book warns that by confirmation price may already be far from the extreme, so reward:risk must be evaluated.
quote: Since short covering equals buying, and bulls will also be buying, it provides fuel for a rally.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Hammer / Umbrella Lines, pp.30-35
notes: Hanging man is the exact SHORT mirror after an advance; the book treats the two as one umbrella-line family. The short-covering-fuel mechanism is directly relevant to leveraged perps where liquidation-driven wick extremes and forced covering are core microstructure. Distinct from existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim: it needs no prior extreme reference, only a long lower wick after a directional move.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Opposite-color body engulfing reversal (incl. dark cloud cover / piercing as depth variants)
mechanism: A longer opposite-color body that fully swallows the prior body shows an abrupt intraday takeover by the other side; the deeper the intrusion into the prior body, the stronger the reversal signal.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, after a directional move, a bar of the opposite color has a real body that completely surrounds the prior bar's real body (engulfing). Strengthening factors: a steep/long prior move, a tiny first body (spinning top or doji), a long shaven second body, and heavy volume. Dark cloud cover (bearish) and piercing (bullish) are weaker two-bar depth variants requiring the second body to close at least halfway into the first body after a gap-up/gap-down open.
trigger_invalidation: Not engulfing if the second body does not fully surround the first body (becomes dark cloud/piercing if at least half); if opens match at both ends the bodies are equal and criteria fail. A prior directional move is required.
risk_geometry: Entry near the close of the engulfing bar or on the next bar's open; stop at the failure point (low of the bullish engulfing bar / high of the bearish one); target at structure (overhead resistance). Book stresses that by confirmation price may already be well off the extreme, so reward:risk must justify the entry.
quote: The engulfing pattern exemplifies an abrupt turnaround in investor psychology.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Engulfing Patterns, pp.55-59
notes: Book ranks engulfing as a stronger signal than dark cloud cover / piercing. A single body_intrusion_reversal family parameterized by depth-of-intrusion (>=50% vs full engulf) spans all three, consistent with the V8 variants rule. Heavy-volume strengthening maps to the participation feature group.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Doji reversal after a directional move (northern doji at top)
mechanism: A bar whose open and close are at/near the same price (no body) after a directional move signals intraday equilibrium/indecision that cannot sustain the move, warning of a direction change.
setup_summary: After an advance, a bar forms whose open and close are at or very near the same price (no real body); this is a bearish northern doji, strongest after one or more long bullish bars. After a decline it is a weaker bullish southern doji. Long-legged / dragonfly / gravestone variants encode the same indecision with long shadows and higher volatility.
trigger_invalidation: If the following bar moves in the trend direction the signal is negated; the book cautions a doji is a warning, not a guarantee, and loses potency in declining markets.
risk_geometry: Book recommends waiting for confirmation before entering (especially for southern doji); the doji's high/low acts as near-term resistance/support in the book's own examples (doji high repelled price for several sessions); no target from the pattern itself.
quote: The doji represents indecision, which is not likely to sustain a move.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Doji, pp.41-45
notes: The book itself says the doji is over-credited and is more reliable at tops than bottoms. On continuous 24h data, open-close parity is more arbitrary than on session-based markets (book: intraday opens/closes are less significant), so treat as a weak single-bar variant rather than a standalone active expert given the complexity budget.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Gap classification, fill tendency, and gap zones as support/resistance
mechanism: Markets dislike voids: price tends to return to untraded gap zones; the start of an upside gap (prior bar high) becomes support and the start of a downside gap (prior bar low) becomes resistance.
setup_summary: Detect void gaps between consecutive bars (upside: current low > prior high; downside: current high < prior low). Classify by context: area gap (inside a range, fills fast, little significance), breakaway gap (out of a range, needs heavy volume), continuation/runaway gap (mid-trend, marks roughly the halfway point), exhaustion gap (climax, heavy volume, fills fast, often followed by reversal). Use the gap region or its origin-bar edge as a location zone: a return into an upside gap should find support; a close below the gap breaks that support and turns bearish.
trigger_invalidation: Book warns a continuation vs exhaustion gap cannot be classified at formation time — it takes at least one more bar; a gap is considered filled when most of the void is closed, not necessarily all; some gaps are never filled.
risk_geometry: Gap bottom/top is a stop-relevant level; book example: a stock gapping +35% then pulling back to the gap bottom was a ~24% round trip, which would blow a 15% max-stop; traders must size stops to survive a gap fill or exit into the gap.
quote: The market does not like voids on a chart so there is a strong tendency for gaps to be filled.
chapter_anchor: Ch 8, When Has a Price Gap Been Filled?, p.157; Ch 9, Gaps May Provide Support or Resistance, pp.183-185
notes: The book explicitly states morning gaps occur on stocks 'but not on the charts of continuous 24-hour futures' — the daily-auction gap mechanics do not transfer to perps. What survives is the fill tendency and gap zones as location features between bars (visible on daily/weekly candles in crypto). Low priority; the morning-gap intraday strategy itself is not applicable.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Spurious-pattern rejection (data-snooping guard)
setup_summary: Before promoting any discovered pattern or expert to the registry, demonstrate it discriminates beyond a data-snooping-controlled null: a pattern must NOT appear at comparable frequency on synthetic/randomized tapes. Skinner's pigeons developed elaborate rain-dance rituals to random food delivery; humans map A->B causation by default.
trigger_invalidation: A candidate pattern/expert is rejected if it fires as frequently on shuffled or simulated random tapes as on the real tape.
risk_geometry: Screening protocol, not a trade.
quote: He programmed it to deliver food at random to the famished birds. He saw quite astonishing behavior on the part of the birds; they developed an extremely sophisticated rain-dance type of behavior
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'The Skinner Pigeon Experiment' (p. 178-179); see note 8 citing Sullivan, Timmermann, White 1999 on data-snooping/bootstrap
notes: Controlled experiment (Skinner 1948) plus the cited data-snooping bootstrap literature make this falsifiable. Mandates a random-tape null in V8's lab screening before any PROPOSED->FORMALIZED promotion.

strategy_name: Data snooping / backtest overfitting as survivorship in rule space
mechanism: Trying many parameterizations on history guarantees a spurious past winner; a random series always presents some detectable pattern, so rules that survive are survivors, not genuine edge
setup_summary: Methodology: iterating a rule's parameters until it 'works' on past data ('buy NASDAQ if close more than 1.83% above prior-week average', then 1.2%, then more complex rules) is the same as looking for the survivor within the set of rules. The book cites Sullivan, Timmerman and White: if enough parameterizations are tried over time, some will look superior by pure luck even with no true predictive power. V8 consequence: parameter variants are one multiplicity unit and must be judged on frozen OOS not used in fitting, with the full variant count disclosed.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any rule judged on past data. Invalid: rule fails to hold on frozen OOS; performance collapses when the snooping-adjusted significance (cohort of variants tried) is computed.
risk_geometry: n/a — methodology lesson, no trade geometry.
quote: The more I try, the more I am likely, by mere luck, to find a rule that worked on past data. A random series will always present some detectable pattern.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, The Backtester (p. 134-135)
notes: Also covers the birthday-paradox / cancer-cluster / spurious-correlation argument ('I am convinced that there exists a tradable security... 100% correlated with the changes in temperature in Oulan Bator'). Directly supports V8's multiplicity-unit rule and the challenger + frozen-OOS + registry protocol (rule 15/14).

strategy_name: Lucas critique / non-stationarity: detectable patterns get arbitraged away
mechanism: The data-generating process is non-stationary (a 'mischievous child' replaces the balls), and any pattern detectable to everyone is ironed out as soon as it is acted upon
setup_summary: Methodology: the mischievous-child/urn argument shows inference from a single past time series is shaky when the process changes; the Lucas critique shows any publicly detectable pattern (e.g., Monday effect) is arbitraged away by anticipatory buying, so 'there is no point searching for patterns that are available to everyone with a brokerage account.' For V8: expect decay in any simple, widely-known pattern; test stationarity explicitly and re-validate experts on frozen OOS; treat 'it has never happened before' as no evidence at all (the market-never-drops-20%-in-a-quarter example is unfalsifiable by confirmation).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern-based expert. Invalid: pattern returns decay as participation/volume on it grows; OOS performance erodes while in-sample held.
risk_geometry: n/a — methodology lesson.
quote: If rational traders detect a pattern of stocks rising on Mondays, then, immediately such a pattern becomes detectable, it would be ironed out by people buying on Friday in anticipation of such an effect.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, A Mischievous Child Replaces the Black Balls (p. 97-98)
notes: Crypto TA and funding/fee patterns are widely shared and crowd quickly. Pairs with the black-swan asymmetry: 'our knowledge about the absence of red balls will increase very slowly... our knowledge of the presence of red balls will dramatically improve once one of them is found' — supports falsification (data disproves, never proves), which is V8's constitution (rule 12 evidence-bound, rule 15 frozen OOS).

strategy_name: Collective behavior patterns repeat with statistical reliability (basis for edges)
mechanism: a finite group of traders repeats behavior patterns; groups interacting consistently form collective patterns that are observable, quantifiable, and statistically reliable, giving a pattern-based edge its probability
setup_summary: Edges exist because individuals and groups of traders form behavior patterns that repeat with statistical reliability and occur in every timeframe, so technical analysis can organize collective behavior into patterns that indicate a higher probability of one direction over another. This is the epistemic justification for defining an edge as repeatable pattern + direction, testable via out-of-sample frequency.
trigger_invalidation: Falsifiable: if a candidate pattern's OOS frequency no longer exceeds its base rate, the edge is dead.
risk_geometry: n/a — foundation for edge definition.
quote: These behavior patterns are observable and quantifiable, and they repeat themselves with statistical reliability.
chapter_anchor: Ch 1, 'The Shift to Technical Analysis'
notes: Asserted without data in the book; V8's lab is the vehicle to test whether any specific pattern repeats OOS. Crypto caveat: participant mix and microstructure (leverage, funding, 24/7) change faster than the equity/futures population the book describes, so pattern stability is an empirical question, not an assumption.
book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

strategy_name: Bullish/Bearish Engulfing Pattern
mechanism: The second opposite-color real body fully enveloping the prior body shows buying (bullish) or selling (bearish) pressure overwhelming the prior session's force; the pattern's low/high becomes a frozen support/resistance anchor.
setup_summary: In a clearly definable trend (even short-term), a second candle whose real body engulfs the prior real body and is the opposite color is a reversal signal: bullish engulfing after a decline (LONG), bearish engulfing after a rally (SHORT). Importance rises when the first day is a spinning top, the second body is very long, the move was protracted/fast, or volume is heavy on the second body.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close of the second bar completes the engulfing (body wraps prior body, opposite color, trend required). Invalidation: close below the low of a bullish engulfing pattern voids its support; a black body wrapping a white body after a decline is NOT a bearish engulfing (context-dependence - same shape after a rally only).
risk_geometry: Entry at the second-candle close or on a correction to the pattern low; stop below the lowest low of the bullish pattern / above the highest high of the bearish pattern (pattern acts as support/resistance - frozen refs); targets from Western tools since candles give none.
quote: Two candles comprise the engulfing pattern. The second real body must engulf the prior real body... I use the high of the two candle lines that make the bearish engulfing pattern. That high becomes our resistance... the lowest low of that pattern should become support.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, Reversal Patterns - The Engulfing Pattern, pp. 42-49
notes: Engulfing is the most machine-recognizable candle signal and heavily used in crypto. The pattern-as-support/resistance ref gives a deterministic risk_geometry in V8's frozen-ref style, closely analogous to how failed_breakout freezes prior_high_ref.
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

strategy_name: COT Signal Retry After Fake-Out
mechanism: a prior invalidated signal (fake-out) does not kill the thesis; a fresh major COT signal coinciding with a developing top/bottom formation warrants a second entry attempt
setup_summary: After a COT short (long) signal was faked out and price kept rising (falling), take the second short (long) attempt when a fresh major COT signal appears together with a developing top (bottom) formation. Copper, Oct 1 2007: the first major COT sell signal in ~4 years plus a developing top formation justified another short entry attempt despite the earlier fake-out during the record-breaking rally.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fresh major COT signal + top/bottom formation. Invalidation: no formation develops or price makes a new trend extreme.
risk_geometry: Entry at formation confirmation (new short/long); stop beyond the formation extreme; no explicit R-multiple or expiry given.
quote: Bears should not let the prior fake-out prevent another short entry attempt if a top formation develops.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'Copper Flashes a COT Sell Signal' (Fig. E.3)
notes: Structurally similar to V8 sweep-and-retry / failed-breakout retry logic, but the confirmatory input here is a positioning-climax signal rather than pure price structure.

strategy_name: Expertise in one repeating behavior pattern before broadening
mechanism: More information is not better in trading; limiting awareness to one mechanical behavior pattern builds confidence and accuracy, while information overload from many patterns leads to confusion and losses.
setup_summary: Choose one simple, preferably mechanical, trading system that identifies one behavior pattern that repeats with some degree of frequency; understand every relationship between its components and its profit potential; avoid all other information and opportunities; trade one market, at most two.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology guidance, not a market setup. Book: stay with the exercise until it becomes 'second nature', then and only then broaden.
risk_geometry: n/a
quote: become an expert at just one particular type of behavior pattern that repeats itself with some degree of frequency
chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Three: Becoming an Expert at Just One Market Behavior', pp.171-172
notes: Independent corroboration of V8's expert ontology: one Expert per behavior family, the complexity budget (max 3 active), and the absence of a shared scorer/ranker. Also notes perception and execution are separate skills - a thesis can be perceived and still not executed.

strategy_name: Engulfing / dark-cloud cover / piercing (body-penetration reversal continuum)
mechanism: reversal strength scales with how deeply the second opposite-color body penetrates the first body - partial (dark-cloud/piercing) vs full (engulfing) solar eclipse
setup_summary: Two-bar pattern in a clearly definable trend: (a) bullish/bearish engulfing - second real body of opposite color engulfs the prior real body (shadows need not be engulfed); (b) dark-cloud cover at tops - second bar opens above the prior high and closes >50% into the prior white body; (c) piercing at bottoms - second bar opens under the prior low and closes >50% into the prior black body. Penetration depth is the ordinal strength signal (engulfing > dark-cloud; piercing must exceed the midpoint, on-neck/in-neck/thrusting below-midpoint variants are bearish). Strength factors: small-then-large body pair, after protracted or very fast move, heavy volume on second bar.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern forms in a definable trend. Invalidation: 'If a long, white real body closes above the highs of the dark-cloud cover, or the bearish engulfing pattern, it could presage another rally'; closing under the lows of a bullish engulfing/piercing via a long black candle resumes the downleg.
risk_geometry: Entry: after second-bar close / next bar. Stop: for dark-cloud, 'a benchmark to place a stop - at the new high of the second day of the dark-cloud cover pattern'; for the engulfing pair, beyond the engulfing bar's extreme. Target: not stated. No expiry.
quote: The greater the degree of penetration of the black real body's close into the prior white real body, the greater the chance for a top.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'Engulfing Pattern' pp.38-43, 'Dark-cloud Cover' pp.43-48, 'Piercing Pattern' pp.48-54
notes: Key V8-relevant nuance: engulfing can flag a top WITHOUT a new high being made (the book shows this repeatedly - 'it may give a reversal signal not available using the criteria for a reversal day'), i.e. the pattern is not dependent on gapped opens which are rare in continuous 24/7 markets. The >50% midpoint penetration threshold is a clean, testable parameter. Book notes the bullish engulfing at a downtrend bottom is one of its strongest signals - comparable to failed_breakout but in the opposite (bottom) direction.
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

strategy_name: Change of polarity (old support becomes resistance / old resistance becomes support)
mechanism: traders are emotionally attached to their entry price; when a tested level breaks, trapped buyers become sellers on retests, flipping the level's polarity
setup_summary: Old support, once broken, converts to new resistance and old resistance converts to new support; potency is proportional to the number of times the level was tested and the volume/open interest at each test. The mechanism is explicitly psychological: three buyer groups (bargain hunters, stopped-out longs seeking vindication, adders) all re-enter at the old level; once it breaks, those same groups become sellers at the level. Tradeable form: a flipped level retested with a confirming candlestick (hammer at old-resistance-now-support; the book's silver example: support A,B,C,D broke, rallies to ~$5.33 were used to exit longs).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a historically multi-tested level that price closes through, then returns to. Invalidation: a clean close back through the flipped level in the direction of the old trend (e.g., old resistance re-taken above re-bullishes).
risk_geometry: Entry: on the retest with candlestick confirmation. Stop: beyond the flipped level or the signal-candle extreme. Target: next structure; book pairs polarity with 50% retracements to set targets (orange-juice example: support expected at $1.65 = 50% correction AND prior resistance).
quote: The most important price on any chart is the price at which you entered the market.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'The Change of Polarity Principle' pp.201-207 (psychology explanation p.204-205)
notes: This is the core location-family feature for V8: a 'tested-level count' and 'prior-support-flipped' feature belong in marketstate's location group, and it upgrades stop/target placement for failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim (old level = new magnet). The potency claim (number of tests + volume at tests) is falsifiable. strategy_name: Retracement levels (50%/38%/62%) as confluence resistance/support for candlestick entries
mechanism: retracements of the prior swing act as psychological magnets; resistance/support is expected at the level and is confirmed when a bearish/bullish candlestick forms there
setup_summary: Compute 38%/50%/62% retracements of the last swing (50% is the most-widely-monitored). Expect resistance in a bear market / support in a bull market at the level, and require a candlestick reversal indicator at that level to act (book's gold example: 50% retracement of A-B at $464 -> bearish engulfing at $469 within $5 -> next leg lower; crude oil: 50% of rally at $29.05 -> hammer at $28.30 -> $5 rally). When the trend is strong and a level is pierced, escalate to the next deeper retracement (50% of the larger move) - the book shows a 50% of the whole 1987-89 decline at $430 stopping gold at $425 with harami + hanging man. Confluence with old levels (change of polarity) and moving averages increases reliability.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches a retracement level and a bearish/bullish candlestick pattern forms there. Invalidation: a close through the level (the book would then escalate to the next retracement of the larger move).
risk_geometry: Entry: on the candlestick confirmation at the level. Stop: beyond the level (e.g., past the $464 zone in the gold example). Target: retracement levels can also project targets (measured move from double bottom). No expiry.
quote: Thus, at $464 you look for resistance and confirmation of resistance with a bearish candlestick indicator.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Candlesticks with Retracement Levels' pp.209-214 (50% rule p.210, 'a 32% retracement is where first resistance is sometimes seen' p.175)
notes: Retracement levels are best treated as a feature (level-distance feature in the location group: distance to 50/38/62% of a frozen swing) consumed by entry confirmation, not as an expert - the book itself frames them as 'look for resistance AND confirmation with a bearish candlestick indicator', i.e. the candlestick is the trigger. MEDIUM for crypto: levels are magnets but heavily arbitraged; the 50%-of-larger-move escalation is a useful regime nuance.

strategy_name: Two-bar candlestick reversals (engulfing, harami, hanging man, doji) with next-bar confirmation
mechanism: the reversal bar only becomes a signal when the next session confirms by closing in the reversal direction
setup_summary: Pattern definitions are precise: bullish engulfing = white body engulfs prior black body in a downtrend; bearish engulfing = black body engulfs prior white body in an uptrend; harami = small body inside a large prior body ('truce'); a hanging man or hammer only becomes bearish/bullish with next-session confirmation (e.g., a black session with a lower close). Doji after a long white body is a top warning; doji is more significant at tops than bottoms.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern at an extended zone (uptrend/downtrend location). Hanging-man/doji/hammer variants require next-bar confirmation before acting; invalidated if the confirmation session does not follow through or if the pattern's extreme is violated.
risk_geometry: Entry on the confirmation bar close. Book example (corn): buy at $2.68 with stop under support at $2.64, target downward-sloping resistance at $2.79; earlier example moved stop to breakeven when a nearer resistance stalled the move.
quote: A hanging man... signals the market has become vulnerable, but there should be bearish confirmation the next session (i.e., a black candlestick session with a lower close or a weaker opening) to signal a top.
chapter_anchor: Glossary A (engulfing, harami, hanging man, doji, pp. 289-301); Ch. 20 corn/coffee trade examples (pp. 284-286); Ch. 15 bonds doji-tweezers bottom (p. 243)
notes: Representative of the book's whole reversal-pattern family (engulfing/harami/doji/hammer/morning-evening star are all precisely defined in Glossary A). The distinct falsifiable claims: (1) pattern + next-bar confirmation beats pattern alone, and (2) patterns are context-conditional ('doji days are usually more significant as reversals in uptrends than in downtrends'). Part 1 likely covers the pure pattern definitions; this finding anchors the confirmation and context requirements.

strategy_name: Change of polarity - old support becomes resistance (and vice versa)
mechanism: a defended level that breaks leaves both a vacuum and a positional memory; price that returns to the level finds the former defenders as counterparties
setup_summary: A zone that acted as support acts as resistance once broken (and conversely). Coffee example: late-March/May lows near $0.92 broke on June 14; the brief rally stopped exactly at $0.92, confirming the flipped zone, and a short was taken on June 21 when price failed to clear the window resistance, with a stop above $0.9175 and a $0.8675 objective.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price stalls/rejects at a former-support-now-resistance (or former-resistance-now-support) zone, preferably with a bearish (bullish) candlestick at the zone. Invalidated if price closes back through the zone to the prior side (flip failed).
risk_geometry: Entry on rejection at the flipped zone (close/confirmation); stop beyond the zone/reference extreme; target = the next prior support level. Book uses a window high as the stop reference.
quote: Remember the axiom that old support can become resistance. The late March and May lows were near $.92... This level became resistance.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 20 coffee example (pp. 283-284); Glossary B 'Change of polarity' (p. 303); Ch. 7 references (pp. 201-207)
notes: Cleanly transferable: perp price levels are not distorted by overnight gaps, so polarity-flip zones are a natural 'location' feature for MarketState. Could later form a standalone location-based expert (entry on rejection at a flipped zone), but the book's evidence is case-study only.

strategy_name: Big Belt week-open key-reversal candle
mechanism: Weekend-reopening excitement overshoots the fair price; the reversal candle prints on a zone with the open beyond the prior close and the close at the opposite extreme, marking an exhaustion high/low.
setup_summary: On a zone, a candle opens beyond the previous candle's close and closes at the opposite extreme: bearish belt opens near the high and closes near the low; bullish belt opens near the low and closes near the high. In forex these nearly always surface on the first trading day of the week. Enter via a sell stop below the low (bearish) / buy stop above the high (bullish); stop on the other side; target the next zone. Book claims an 'exceptionally high win rate' on daily charts and recommends the daily timeframe.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: zone + open-beyond-prior-close candle with the close at the opposite extreme; room to the left preferred. Invalidation: stop beyond the opposite extreme; trade never triggers if the market does not trade beyond the belt's entry level.
risk_geometry: Entry: sell stop below the low (bearish belt) / buy stop above the high (bullish belt). Stop: a few pips beyond the opposite extreme. Target: nearest zone. Timeframe gate: daily recommended.
quote: bearish big belts nearly always surface on the first trading day of the week. The market opens much higher than the closing price of the previous week and then steadily trades lower
chapter_anchor: Ch.9 'The Big Belt' pp.151-161 (characteristics pp.160-161)
notes: The week-open gap premise does not exist in 24/7 crypto perps (no weekly close). The candle-shape reversal at a zone could feed the candlestick family, but the catalyst trigger (first day of the week after a weekend pause) is forex-specific and the 'high win rate' claim is untested narrative.

strategy_name: Engulfing reversal at support with volume confirmation
mechanism: an engulfing candle at a support location shows aggressive directional absorption; heavier volume and support confluence raise its significance
setup_summary: A bullish engulfing candle (white body fully engulfs prior black body) that forms at a chart-support location (prior low, trendline, or moving average) with above-average volume is a short-term reversal signal; bearish engulfing is symmetric at resistance. Falsifiable on 1h BTC: engulfing-at-support on rising volume precedes short-term reversals more often than engulfing in mid-range on average volume.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: engulfing candle closing at a support/resistance location on above-average volume. Invalidation: next bar closes back through the engulfing body (failed reversal).
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the engulfing bar (bar-close entry). Stop: below engulfing low (bullish) / above engulfing high (bearish). Target: not stated; book presents it as a short-term turn tool to be combined with other criteria.
quote: If that short-term upside reversal takes place in an area of chart support (like a previous low, a trendline, or a moving average), it takes on even more significance. Heavier upside volume also adds to the significance of the pattern.
chapter_anchor: Appendix B, 'Bullish Engulfing Pattern' (figs B.3-B.5); candlestick reversal list indexed under 'Bullish Reversal Patterns'

strategy_name: Reversal candlesticks at support/resistance after extended moves (hammer, shooting star, doji, engulfing, harami cross)
mechanism: single or multi-candle rejection at a prior price extreme reveals order-flow exhaustion and a reversal of short-term direction; the more prior candles a benchmark candle engulfs, the stronger the signal
setup_summary: After an extended trend or near prior S/R/pivot levels require a reversal candle: hammer (lower shadow at least 2x body, body at upper end, little/no upper shadow) at support; shooting star (long upper shadow, body low, little/no lower shadow) at resistance; doji after a long white candle near a top; bearish/bullish engulfing covering the prior body; bearish harami cross (long white candle then doji inside its body) after a long advance. Enter on next-bar confirmation; tops need more confirmation than bottoms ('tops take longer to form than bottoms' - look for a SECOND bearish candle at resistance).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reversal candle completes within 1-2 bars of a prior extreme; bullish patterns require next-candle validation (e.g., inverted hammer needs a white candle opening above it). Thesis invalidation: close beyond the pattern extreme; failure of next-bar confirmation.
risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR after confirmation; stop beyond the candle extreme (for hammer below the low, close-only per book); target = prior structure (pivot S1/R1, trendline, or candle midpoint as first support for 'pillar of strength'); expiry = 2-3 bars intraday, longer on weekly charts.
quote: The lower part, or the shadow, should be at least twice the length of the real body... The more candles that are engulfed, the more power behind the signal!

notes: Nison-style practitioner patterns, anecdotal evidence. On 1h BTCUSDT these shapes are computable and common; high leverage manufactures long wicks (sweeps) that form hammer/shooting-star shapes, which cuts both ways (patterns fire on liquidity sweeps that may continue). Best consumed as a behavior family on top of location features (prior extreme / pivot).

strategy_name: Fibonacci retracements, extensions and projected targets (confluence with pivots)
mechanism: price corrections and extensions cluster at Fibonacci ratios (0.382/0.50/0.618/0.786 retracements; 1.272/1.618 extensions) because orders concentrate there; projected targets = move length x ratio added to the retracement point
setup_summary: After an initial A-to-B move, a pullback to C: ratios 0.382/0.50/0.618/0.786 of the A-B move define support/resistance zones. Upside projections = A-B length x (0.618 / 1.00 / 1.618 / 2.618) added to point C (or retracement level). When a Fibonacci target coincides with a pivot R1/S1 or a prior MA crossover, the confluence is treated as a high-probability reaction/exit point. 100% retracement = double bottom retest; 1.272/1.618 extensions project support below a broken initial low.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price pulls back into a ratio zone with reversal-candle or momentum confirmation. Thesis invalidation: ratio zone fails - price exceeds the 0.786 retracement (trend likely over) or breaks the 1.272 extension.
risk_geometry: entry at the ratio zone with confirmation; stop beyond the ratio (below 0.786 retracement / above 1.618 extension); target = the projected extension or a coincident pivot level; expiry = swing.
quote: If you apply a Fibonacci ratio multiplier of 1.272 percent or 1.618 percent of the initial move, you can determine potential support beneath the market once it has taken out the initial low.
chapter_anchor: Ch 8, 'Fibonacci Numbers'
notes: No statistical backing in the book (anecdotal; author notes 'uncanny coincidence' with pivot calculations). Best role in V8: a location feature-group input that enriches the existing location features with ratio-derived S/R candidates, and as confluence for the pivot_reversal family - not a standalone expert. Difficulty flagged by the book itself: identifying the peaks and troughs to measure from.
